source.version: Author manuscript dated January 21, 2026 (title page), deposited at AIR UNIMI as MS20241460-main-20251208.pdf; main text and references only (19 pages), no appendices; the journal version of record is The Economic Journal advance article doi 10.1093/ej/ueag015. Read from the PDF on file.

supplement.where: Supplementary Material and Appendix A (p. 5); Appendices B1 and B2 (p. 5, fn. 6; p. 6, fn. 8); Appendix B3 (p. 13, fn. 14); Appendix C: Figure C1 (p. 6, Section 2.2), Table C1 (p. 8), Table C2 and Figure C2 (p. 9, Section 2.3), Table C3 (p. 13), and Tables C4-C7 (p. 15, Section 4). Not included in this PDF.
supplement.holds: Experimental protocols and instructions (Supplementary Material, Appendices B1-B3), example AI and human answers (Appendix A), distribution of creativity scores (Figure C1), rater-demographics regressions (Table C1), LDA topic words (Table C2), frequency of originality, elaboration and nonsense themes in raters' written explanations (Figure C2), creative-style robustness (Table C3), and GPT-as-evaluator results (Tables C4-C7).

paper_design_summary: The authors took 40 human answers per task from the participants of Charness and Grieco (2019), one closed task (a creative story using ten mandatory words) and one open task (what would you invent and why), and generated 40 answers per task with GPT-3.5 (Session I, July 2023), GPT-4o (Session II, October 2024), and GPT-4.5 (Session III, April 2025). In each session, Prolific raters who did not know that some answers came from AI each scored six randomly drawn answers (three human, three AI) for creativity on a 1-10 scale; in Sessions II and III they also scored originality, elaboration, and nonsense. No person used AI to produce an answer.

studies.label: Session I (GPT-3.5 answers vs human answers, July 2023)

assignment.prereg_locator: p. 1, title-page footnote; AsPredicted #136955, https://aspredicted.org/HMT_X2P (public PDF: https://aspredicted.org/z8gd5.pdf), p. 1, header and question 3, read in memory. The manuscript reports June 26, 2023; the registration PDF states June 27, 2023. This discrepancy is unresolved.

participants.who: Raters recruited on Prolific (738 across the three sessions, p. 4). Table 1 (p. 7) lists 128 raters in the Closed sub-session and 123 in the Open sub-session of Session I; the text gives 1506 evaluations in Session I (p. 5). The scored outputs are 40 human answers per task from Charness and Grieco (2019) participants (tournament incentives) and 40 GPT-3.5 answers per task. The human producers were laboratory students from Charness and Grieco (2019)'s Tournament treatment; they were distinct from the Prolific evaluators (pp. 5-6, Section 2.1 and fns. 6, 8; p. 15, Section 5).
participants.quote: the experimental subjects are standard laboratory subjects (students) and were not made aware in advance of the topic of the experiment
participants.locator: p. 4, Section 2.1 (raters and sessions); pp. 5-6, Section 2.1 and fns. 6, 8 (human-answer source and incentives); p. 7, Table 1 (rater counts); p. 15, Section 5 (student producers)

ai_tool.how_used: AI generated answers on its own (no human used it): prompt identical to the human task instruction, temperature varied from 0 to 2 with the same values across tasks and versions, length parameter raised to 400 (p. 5).

task.description: Two tasks. Closed: 'Write a creative story using compulsorily the following words: house, zero, forgive, curve, relevance, cow, tree, planet, ring, send.' (creative writing). Open: 'If you had the talent to invent things just by thinking of them, what would you create and why?' (idea generation). Raters scored each answer for creativity on a 1-10 scale (pp. 5-6).

outcomes.name: Creativity score, closed task
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Blind Prolific raters' 1-10 creativity score; Table 1 averages each rater's scores of the three human and three AI answers; Table 2 is OLS of the average score on AI, Open, AI x Open and temperature, errors clustered at the subject-response level, with subject-FE and Romano-Wolf MHT variants. Creativity is the manuscript's main outcome (p. 4, fn. 3) and a preregistered key dependent variable (AsPredicted #136955, p. 1, question 3; https://aspredicted.org/z8gd5.pdf). Table 1 prints means, standard errors and rater counts, not standard deviations (p. 7).

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Charness and Grieco (2019), 'Creativity and incentives', Journal of the European Economic Association 17(2), pp. 454-496. Human answers come from that study's Tournament treatment. S1-S3 reuse the same human-answer pools, so their human benchmarks overlap.
sample_overlap.quote: The 40 answers taken from Charness and Grieco (2019) correspond to the 40 answers in the verbal closed task produced by subjects receiving the Tournament treatment.
sample_overlap.locator: p. 5, Section 2.1 and fn. 6; p. 6, Section 2.1 and fn. 8; p. 17, references

eligibility.reason: No person was assigned generative-AI assistance: GPT answers are compared with earlier human answers (pp. 4-6, Section 2.1). Creativity and originality are scored on those outputs by blind human raters, meeting criterion 3 (p. 5, Section 2.1; pp. 7-9, Tables 1-3). The manuscript reports 40 human participants per task but does not state the unique number of human producers across tasks; fn. 8 also reports five open-task answers excluded for illegible scans (pp. 5-6). Criterion 2 remains unclear; the 738 recruited people are evaluators, not producers (p. 4, Section 2.1; p. 5, fn. 5). This is AI-versus-human context, with no output-diversity measure.

one_line_finding: Blind Prolific raters scored GPT answers higher than human answers on the closed story task (Session I 6.136 vs 5.331, II 6.982 vs 5.936, III 7.417 vs 6.021) and lower on the open invention task (5.108 vs 6.266, 5.933 vs 6.451, 6.451 vs 6.927), with AI x Open coefficients of -1.943, -1.563, and -1.875 (all p < 0.01) (p. 7, Table 1; p. 8, Table 2).
notes: Rater counts: Table 1 Subj. columns sum to 251, 238, and 241 per session (730), while the text gives 738 recruits and 1506, 1482, and 1440 evaluations (pp. 4-5, p. 7). The Session III evaluation count is labelled 'in the second' on p. 5. Answers were drawn at random for each rater (p. 4); the text does not say how raters were allocated to the Closed or Open sub-session. Human answers come from Charness and Grieco (2019); footnote 8 (p. 6) says five open-task answers were excluded for illegible scans while the text says 40 answers per task. Preregistered at AsPredicted #136955, #194851, #225528 (p. 1 footnote). Section 4 (GPT as evaluator) results sit in Appendix Tables C4-C7, not in this PDF. Table 2 errors are clustered at the subject-response level.
